title: Ecclesiastes Bible Quiz - Chapter 9
description: Ten questions on Ecclesiastes 9: one event that comes to all, eating bread with joy, time and chance, and the poor wise man who delivered a city.

questions.text: According to this chapter, what is a living dog better than?
questions.explanation: For him who is joined with all the living there is hope, for a living dog is better than a dead lion.

answers.text: A dead lion
A sleeping lion
A caged bird
A strong horse

questions.text: What do the living know, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: The living know that they will die, but the dead don't know anything, neither do they have any more a reward.

answers.text: That their reward is great
That their memory will last forever
That they will die
That love and hatred await them

questions.text: How does the speaker tell the reader to eat his bread and drink his wine?
questions.explanation: The speaker says to eat your bread with joy and drink your wine with a merry heart, for God has already accepted your works.

answers.text: With fasting and mourning
With joy and a merry heart
In silence and fear
Only on feast days

questions.text: What does the speaker say about your garments and your head?
questions.explanation: The speaker says to let your garments be always white, and don't let your head lack oil.

answers.text: Tear your garments to pieces and shave all the hair of your head
Wear purple garments and put a crown of gold on your head
Sell your garments and keep your head covered at all times
Let your garments be always white, and don't let your head lack oil

questions.text: Why should you do with your might whatever your hand finds to do?
questions.explanation: There is no work, nor plan, nor knowledge, nor wisdom in Sheol, where you are going.

answers.text: Because there is no work, plan, knowledge, or wisdom in Sheol
Because the king inspects every man's work
Because the strong take the work of the idle
Because work makes a man rich

questions.text: The race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong. What happens to them all instead?
questions.explanation: Bread is not to the wise, nor riches to men of understanding, nor favor to men of skill, but time and chance happen to them all.

answers.text: Glory and honor come to them all
Death and judgment come to them all
Time and chance happen to them all
Labor and sorrow happen to them all

questions.text: To which creatures are the sons of men compared when an evil time falls suddenly on them?
questions.explanation: As fish taken in an evil net and birds caught in the snare, so are the sons of men snared in an evil time.

answers.text: Sheep without a shepherd and oxen in a field
Fish taken in an evil net and birds caught in the snare
Lions in a den and deer on the mountains
Ants in summer and locusts in winter

questions.text: Who delivered the little city that a great king besieged?
questions.explanation: A poor wise man was found in the city, and he by his wisdom delivered the city, yet no man remembered that same poor man.

answers.text: A young soldier with a sword
A rich merchant with a ransom
A prophet sent by God
A poor wise man, by his wisdom

questions.text: After seeing the poor man's deed, what did the speaker say wisdom is better than?
questions.explanation: The speaker said, "Wisdom is better than strength," though the poor man's wisdom is despised and his words are not heard.

answers.text: Strength
Riches
Beauty
Long life

questions.text: According to the last verse of this chapter, what does one sinner destroy?
questions.explanation: Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good.

answers.text: His own house
The weapons of war
Much good
The city walls
